issues.title: TRansition: ConfigScreenManager.registerConfigScreen is not thread-safe
issues.body:
### What happens
Occasionally (roughly 1 in N launches) Forge fails to construct a mod instance:

java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 1 out of bounds for length 0
    at java.util.ArrayList.add(ArrayList.java:484)
    at dev.tr7zw.transition.manager.ConfigScreenManager.registerConfigScreen(ConfigScreenManager.java:13)
    at dev.tr7zw.transition.loader.ModLoaderUtil.registerConfigScreen(ModLoaderUtil.java:154)
    at dev.tr7zw.skinlayers.SkinLayersModBase.<init>(SkinLayersModBase.java:25)

Restarting always fixes it, which points at a race rather than bad data.

### Why it races
ClientTRansitionMod.configScreenManager is a static singleton, and its
configScreens field is a plain ArrayList. Forge constructs mods on the
modloading-worker thread pool, so when several of your mods are present
(skinlayers3d + firstperson + notenoughanimations + entityculling) they
call registerConfigScreen concurrently and race inside ArrayList.add:

    add(E e) -> add(e, elementData, size)
    // two threads read size==0, one grows, the other writes elementData[1]
    // against the pre-grow array of length 0  ->  index 1, length 0

The reported "Index 1 out of bounds for length 0" matches exactly.

### Suggestion
    private final List<Function<Screen, Screen>> configScreens =
        new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
    // or Collections.synchronizedList(new ArrayList<>())

### Environment
Forge 47.4.26, MC 1.20.1
skinlayers3d 1.11.3 / firstperson 2.7.3 / notenoughanimations 1.12.6 /
entityculling 1.11.3  (TRansition 1.0.25 and 1.0.26 both affected --
the bytecode of ConfigScreenManager is identical in both)

The above content is provided by deepseek

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Separate Voxel Size Slider for Equipped Armor (To prevent clipping with 3D Armor Resource Packs)
issues.body:
**Hi there!** First of all, thank you for this amazing mod. It adds so much life to the game and I’ve been using it since always!!

I am writing to suggest a feature that would greatly improve the experience for players who use custom 3D armor resource packs or custom armors in general. *(I know there is already a solution by making the voxels smaller, but this might make the mod more customizable and open to more options).*


When using some custom 3D armor models, the default 3D skin layers (voxels) often **clip through the armor**, ruining the aesthetic. 

While there is already an option to adjust the voxel size (especially for the head), most players stick to the default voxel size for their normal skin (which should be **1.8** if I remember correctly) and get used to it, just like myself.

However, when putting on armor, the default size is **often too large**. 
Usually, a voxel size around **1.2** is the sweet spot to prevent clipping, but changing it manually every time is not practical, and it doesn’t look as cool as the default voxel size when unarmored.

### Proposed Feature
It would be incredibly helpful to have an option to scale/modify the voxel size **EXCLUSIVELY** when a specific armor piece is equipped. 

Ideally, this would include separate scaling options:
* **Head Voxel Size:** Applied automatically when wearing a helmet.
* **Body Voxel Size:** Applied automatically when wearing a piece of armor that is not the helmet.

This way, the skin looks perfect when unarmored, but automatically scales down slightly to fit cleanly inside custom 3D armor without clipping.



Custom 3D armors are extremely popular right now, especially on multiplayer and roleplay servers where players rely on highly detailed custom gear. Let’s be honest, nowadays almost every server has its own texture pack with custom items, armors included (it often happened to me that the voxels were clipping in custom server armors too, not only personal texture packs). Clipping completely breaks this immersion imo.

To give you an idea of the demand, resource packs featuring 3D armors where clipping happens having default voxel size, have massive user bases. 
Just looking at Modrinth:
* **Armored Legacy** has over **73k** downloads.
* **Armory Conglomery** has over **400k** downloads.

Adding a **"Voxel Scale while armored"** setting would be a huge quality-of-life update for a very large portion of your user base. It would also remove a lot of pain and time waste because people often go to either this Github or the texture pack makers to report the voxels clipping.

Thank you for considering this suggestion and for your hard work on the mod!

Then went outside to the opposite side of that wall but I'm not currently looking at it. If I were to reenable the mod and looked at that wall, even for a split second, it crashes. Then the world continues to crash until I disable to mod. It can't be any of the other mods I have installed since this mod has worked perfectly fine with them for the past year on many different versions (I use CurseForge).

issues.title: Issue with loading Wither Skeleton Skulls
issues.body:
Hello! 

I appear to have run into a bug on 1.21.4 where this mod crashes the game whenever attempting to render the textures for a Wither Skeleton Skull, whether it is in the player's inventory or a chest.  If the skull is in the player's inventory or chest, the game crashes as soon as the respective storage option is opened, and if the skull is in the hotbar, the game crashes immediately upon loading into a world.

I am currently running the game on Fabric 1.21.4 with other mods installed, all client side.  No other currently installed mods and/or resource packs should be affecting the skulls, but I am happy to provide a list of them and/or any crash reports generated during troubleshooting if you think it will be helpful.

**What to do:**
1. Join a world with a Skin that has transparent pixels on the top layer.
2. Select transparent pixels to be emissive in ETF. (Entity Model Features > Textures > Player skin settings > Open skin feature tool > Emissive pixels: ON and "Select pixels")

issues.title: No null check for Minecraft.getInstance().player, causing crash
issues.body:
I've noticed that in `PlayerRendererMixin::setModelProperties` you use `Minecraft.getInstance().player` without a null check.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38552516/168414322-6556bc7a-eeaf-4d90-ada9-767b4f235b69.png)

Normally this wouldn't be a problem, since no players will get rendered unless the user has a world loaded. However, this causes issues when a mod tries to render a PlayerEntity while no world is loaded, which [one of my mods](https://github.com/enjarai/show-me-your-skin) does. See crash report [here](https://github.com/enjarai/show-me-your-skin/files/8692164/crash-2022-05-10_14.56.21-client.txt).

This could likely be fixed very easily by adding a null check that either: cancels the method, or preferably, skips the distance check that causes the issue.

issues.title: Two skulls with the same UUID / name can have different skins, but 3D Skin Layers does not account for this.
issues.body:
Steps to reproduce:

1. `/give @p player_head{SkullOwner:"(your name)"}`
2. Place that skull in the world.
3. Exit Minecraft.
4. Change your skin.
5. Enter Minecraft.
6. `/give @p player_head{SkullOwner:"(your name)"}`
7. Place that skull in the world.
8. Note that the 3D layers are incorrect on one of the skulls.

Diagnosis:

GameProfile#equals considers two profiles to be equal if the name and UUID match, however skulls store the full GameProfile in their NBT, which includes all of the cached texture links. This means that when the user changes their skin, the skull maintains its appearance from when it was created.

This means that for skulls, it is not possible to correctly associate 3D head layer data to a GameProfile / UUID - rather, it must be associated to a texture location, whether that is the texture location stored in the NBT, or the ResourceLocation of the texture in TextureManager.

issues.title: Potential memory leak
issues.body:
SkinUtil calls `NativeImage#untrack()`, seemingly in an attempt to deallocate the NativeImage object: https://github.com/tr7zw/3d-Skin-Layers/blob/9b3cc5f5f04dd886eaf8da32534dc92f30107cd7/3dSkinLayers-Shared/src/main/java/dev/tr7zw/skinlayers/SkinUtil.java#L61

However, `NativeImage#untrack()` does not deallocate the texture - rather, it removes it from LWJGL's leak tracking, meaning that not only does this code potentially leak memory, it does so in a way that is invisible to LWJGL's debugging tools.

It seems like you intended to call `NativeImage#close()`.

issues.title: Jacket layer clips with leggings
issues.body:
Steps to reproduce

1. Have a skin which jacket layer intersects with the top part of leggings
2. Wear leggings in game with no chestplate

This bug might also affect other combinations, like armor textures that are bigger than they're intended (ex.: sleeves and gloves for chestplate). On my skin, the sides of the jacket layer clip with the sides of the leggings.
